text: People are all treating this as definitely his retirement message. The thing about some of these chronic illnesses is that you really don't know; it's not like a joint injury where they just look at an MRI and immediately say "you'll be out 9 months but should be able to make a full recovery within a year" or "your joint is busted in a way that ensures you'll never be an athlete again." The causes of CFS related illness are poorly understood and there's no road map. For some people, if they get the right pattern of rest and nutrition and just the right dose of mild exercise, their bodies do eventually get out of the vicious circle and they can return to full activity, but who knows how long it'll take, could be months or decades. For others that never happens. And even if symptoms basically disappear there's the possibility of a relapse. I ended up diagnosed with ME/CFS as a teenager and spent most of high school in bed and had to rely on a walking stick as though I were a nonagenarian. A dozen years later I had recovered so well that I did 100mi bike rides and ran a couple marathons. After I got COVID some -- thankfully not all -- of those old symptoms are back and managing my energy is a real frustration.
